content:
Ellen Park: hey team — during my first-week setup I followed the K8s quickstart but `kubectl get ns training-env` returns "namespaces \"training-env\" not found". I'm on mac and using fish shell; I set KUBECONFIG but not sure if it merged correctly. any tips?

DevEx Sam: welcome Ellen! :wave: fish behaves slightly different with KUBECONFIG. run `echo $KUBECONFIG` in fish (use `set -q KUBECONFIG; and echo $KUBECONFIG`), then `kubectl config get-contexts` and `kubectl config current-context`. Also try `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/okta-config kubectl get ns` to see that file alone.

Ellen Park: thanks. `set -q KUBECONFIG; and echo $KUBECONFIG` outputs `/Users/ellen/.kube/config /Users/ellen/.kube/okta` (space-separated). `kubectl config get-contexts` shows `redwood-dev` and `redwood-ci`, current is `redwood-dev`.

DevEx Sam: ah — fish uses space-separated KUBECONFIG not colon. If your files merged in the wrong order your authinfo might be from a different file. Try exporting with colon for processes that expect it: `env KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/.kube/okta kubectl config view --flatten` OR just `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/okta kubectl get ns` to inspect the okta-only config.

Ellen Park: when I run `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/okta kubectl auth can-i list pods -n training-env` -> "no". I also attempted `kubectl --as=system:serviceaccount:training:dev-sa get pods -n training-env` but got `forbidden: cannot impersonate serviceaccount`.

DevEx Sam: ok that's RBAC. For quick onboarding we can grant a temporary RoleBinding to your Okta principal in `training-env`. For automation we recommend creating an ephemeral service-account token. @eng-infra-bot please open an infra ticket for Ellen training-env access.

eng-infra-bot: Created INFRA-4555: "training-env access for Ellen Park". Assignee: @platform-oncall. ETA 1h.

platform-oncall: Hi Ellen 44b I can apply a 24h RoleBinding to give `edit` in `training-env` to your `ellen@okta`. Would you prefer that or an SA token?

Ellen Park: RoleBinding is great for now — want to finish the walkthrough. Thanks!

platform-oncall: Applied RoleBinding in namespace `training-env` for `ellen@okta`. Run:
```
kubectl auth can-i list pods -n training-env
kubectl get pods -n training-env
```

Ellen Park: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n training-env` -> yes. `kubectl get pods -n training-env` -> shows demo pods, I'm unblocked. Huge thanks! :tada:

DevEx Sam: nice. Quick follow-ups: 1) if you keep using fish, we recommend a tiny wrapper script `export_kube(){ set -x KUBECONFIG ~/.kube/config:~/.kube/okta; kubectl \"$@\" }` or just use `env KUBECONFIG=... kubectl ...` for one-off commands; 2) if you want the SA token flow later ping infra and we can show how to `kubectl create token` and make a dedicated context.

onboarding-bot: 44c K8s access granted and linked INFRA-4555 to ONBOARD-224. Checklist updated.

Ellen Park: marked the checklist. Thanks all for the speedy help!
